Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old female with ~3 weeks of left-sided hearing reduction and left facial numbness, with intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness; remote assessment suggests possible Bell's palsy but requires urgent face-to-face neurological and ear examination today.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Left-sided decreased hearing and left facial numbness for approximately three weeks.
  - Intermittent ringing in the left ear (tinnitus); occasional dizziness associated with the tinnitus.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began about three weeks ago and have been persistent; numbness is present most of the time and was present at time of video visit.
  - Dizziness occurs occasionally, typically when tinnitus is present.
  - Patient reports symptoms have begun to impact work/training (reduced training).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - None specifically identified.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No generalized weakness or numbness elsewhere.
  - No difficulty swallowing.
  - No speech disturbance.
  - No visual problems.
  - No ear discharge.
  - No ear pain.
  - No fever.
  - No ear itchiness.
- Other relevant history from interview:
  - Prior history of nasal polyps; uses a prescription nasal spray intermittently (name not recalled).
  - Patient reports a remote episode she thinks was "labyrinthitis" (patient-reported, not documented).
  - Patient expresses anxiety about severity; clinician provided preliminary reassurance but requested in-person assessment.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps — uses a prescribed nasal spray PRN (name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Patient-reported remote history of labyrinthitis (patient uncertain).
- Medications explicitly mentioned:
  - Nasal spray (prescription) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Rennies (OTC antacid) PRN — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - Latex.

Social History:
- Age/sex: 40-year-old female.
- Occupation: Jockey (works with horses); symptoms have reduced ability to train and impacted work.
- Living situation: Conflict noted in transcript — patient initially said she lives alone then stated she lives with her partner.
- Pets: None.
- Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: Not mentioned.

Family History:
- Brother with neurofibromatosis (patient report).
- Other family history: otherwise reportedly "everyone else is OK" (no further details).

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (remote video consult). Planned face-to-face neurological and ear examination.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or test results documented.
- Plan includes in-clinic neurological exam and otoscopic examination (details below).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided facial numbness with ipsilateral decreased hearing
  - Assessment: Clinician's preliminary impression: possible Bell's palsy (to be confirmed on physical examination). Remote evaluation cannot definitively exclude other causes.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic assessment today for full neurological examination to confirm diagnosis and exclude other pathology.
    - Perform otoscopic examination to assess ear; look for any local ear pathology.
    - General reassurance given that condition is unlikely to be life-threatening based on remote assessment, but in-person assessment required for definitive evaluation.
    - Patient instructed to ensure the clinic appointment occurs today.
- Issue 2: Intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness
  - Assessment: Associated symptoms with primary complaint; etiology to be determined on in-person evaluation.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate tinnitus and dizziness during clinic visit (neurological and ENT assessment).
    - Document symptom frequency and correlation with other findings.
- Issue 3: Nasal polyps / prior labyrinthitis (past history)
  - Assessment: Nasal polyps stable; uses nasal spray PRN. Past labyrinthitis reported but not currently active.
  - Plan:
    - No specific interventions documented for these issues at this visit beyond usual PRN use.
- Administrative / follow-up plan:
  - Doctor to send message to admin team to book patient into a face-to-face clinic in Central London today.
  - Patient advised to call the support team number (to be left in notes) after five minutes so they can slot her into a convenient clinic appointment.
  - Emphasis on attending the in-person appointment today for definitive assessment.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented vital signs.
  - No head/neck or neurological physical examination findings (none performed during video consult).
  - No medication list with doses, routes, frequencies (nasal spray name unknown; Rennies dose/frequency not documented).
  - No laboratory or imaging results.
  - No smoking, alcohol, or substance use history provided.
  - No pregnancy status documented (female, age 40).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Living situation conflict: patient initially said she "lives alone" then corrected to "lives with my partner."
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Overall audio and content were sufficiently clear for clinical extraction; a few details were uncertain or not recalled by the patient (name of nasal spray; exact prior diagnosis of "labyrinthitis" uncertain).
